summary: Brendan S. Gillon specializes in indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1980–1985) and served as Associate Professor in the Department of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, held research and teaching posts at Otani, Shiga, Kwansei Gakuin, and Kyoto universities, and taught philosophy at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Geshe Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under mentor Willis Stoesz (~1982–1986). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018).

Brian Daizen Victoria works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities and Eihei-ji, he held posts at Auckland, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Adelaide (~2004–2015), Antioch (2005–2013), and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (2013).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara (attested 2005) and is attested in 2026 at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an indologist, tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at The King's School, Macclesfield, East India Company College, and Fort William College, he served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (~1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and completed his PhD at Rice University under Anne C. Klein (attested 2011).

Brian Kensho Nagata works in Buddhist studies. He has served as Director of BDK America (attested 2004, 2013), President of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research, and Director at Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (attested 2017).

Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) worked in history, archaeology, and indology. She studied at the University of Cape Town and UCL Institute of Archaeology under Frederick Zeuner, and was later a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978–2017).

Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna (~1980–1984), where she earned her doctorate. She later served as an extraordinary university professor at the University of Vienna from around 1999 to 2022.

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, she studied under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop, and held posts at Auckland, Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn works in sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan under Donald J. Munro, he held posts at Northwestern University (~1999–2012) and the University of Chicago (~2013).
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence specializes in religious studies and indology. Educated at Fay School, Episcopal Divinity School, and Princeton University, he was a professor at Duke University from approximately 1971 to 2011, later becoming professor emeritus.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. His studies included training under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (~1971–1977). He held a post at Yale University (~1985–1987) and served as a director at Bard College from around 1987.
Bruce John Stewart works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and completed his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Bruce Lincoln is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and Chicago (~1993).
